speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your symptoms. To better understand your condition, could you please tell me if you have noticed any changes in your skin, such as jaundice (yellowing of the eyes or skin) or a rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of ulcerative colitis and recent sexual activity, have you noticed any changes in your urine color or stool consistency, such as clay-colored stools or dark urine?

REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel including bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, ALT, AST, and GGT.
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A, B, C, and E serology.
REQUEST TEST: AMA (Antimitochondrial Antibody) and ANA.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdomen ultrasound focusing on the biliary tree and liver architecture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 460 U/L, AST: 75 U/L, ALT: 78 U/L, Anti-Nuclear_Antibody: Negative, Antimitochondrial_Antibodies: Negative, Abdominal_Ultrasound_Findings: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. Hepatitis A, B, C, and E serology: Not reported in provided data. GGT: Not reported in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the elevated alkaline phosphatase, negative viral and autoimmune serologies, and the ultrasound showing biliary dilation, have you recently experienced any fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC).

Given your history of ulcerative colitis and the ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilation, these results are highly characteristic of PSC, which I suspect is the cause of your pruritus and fatigue. I will proceed with this diagnosis as the most likely etiology.
